sec: Craniopharyngioma, Rathke's cleft cyst and acromegaly workup

items.q: Match the craniopharyngioma subtype to its characteristic histological and clinical features — 1) Adamantinomatous type (Childhood, 5–15 yrs, 90%) 2) Papillary type (Adults, 50–74 yrs, 10%) … A) Cystic with machinery oil fluid, wet keratin nodules, calcification ++, T1 hyperintense B) Solid mass, lacking wet keratin or calcification, T1 hypointense
items.exp: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma is childhood cystic with machinery oil, wet keratin, calcification, and T1 hyperintensity; papillary is adult solid and hypointense. (Book p950)

items.q: A 9-year-old boy presents with progressive headache, bitemporal hemianopsia, and polyuria. Cranial CT shows a suprasellar calcified cystic mass. What posterior pituitary complication is produced by stalk compression in craniopharyngioma?
items.exp: Craniopharyngioma compresses the pituitary stalk causing central diabetes insipidus. (Book p950)

items.q: What radiological sign on contrast-enhanced MRI represents the compressed rim of normal pituitary tissue enhancing around a sellar cyst?
items.exp: The claw sign occurs when the rim of compressed normal pituitary takes up contrast around the non-enhancing cystic mass. (Book p950)

items.q: Match the sellar cystic lesion to its histopathological lining — 1) Rathke's cleft cyst 2) Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma … A) Simple columnar or cuboidal epithelium with no calcification B) Squamous epithelium with wet keratin nodules and machinery oil fluid
items.exp: Rathke's cleft cyst is lined by simple columnar epithelium without calcification; adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma has wet keratin and calcification. (Book p950)

items.q: What initial laboratory screening investigation should be ordered for a patient suspected of having acromegaly?
items.exp: Screening for acromegaly is performed by measuring serum IGF-1 levels. (Book p950)

items.q: Following an elevated serum IGF-1 level, what is the definitive confirmatory dynamic test for acromegaly?
opts: Oral glucose suppression test (75 gm glucose) with GH measurement after 1 hour
Insulin tolerance test measuring nadir glucose and peak GH
Glucagon stimulation test measuring GH at 30-minute intervals
Cosyntropin stimulation test measuring cortisol response
items.exp: The diagnostic confirmatory test is the oral glucose suppression test (75 gm glucose) checking GH after 1 hour. (Book p950)

items.q: What nadir growth hormone level 1 hour after a 75 g oral glucose load excludes acromegaly?
items.exp: A nadir GH level < 1 ng/ml on the oral glucose suppression test is normal and excludes acromegaly. (Book p950)

items.q: A post-glucose load growth hormone level exceeding what cutoff indicates very severe disease and a poor prognosis in acromegaly?
items.exp: A GH level > 40 ng/ml following glucose suppression indicates a poor prognosis. (Book p950)

items.q: What is the imaging investigation of choice (IOC) once biochemical acromegaly is confirmed?
items.exp: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI is the imaging investigation of choice for pituitary evaluation in acromegaly. (Book p950)

items.q: The fluid contained within an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma characteristically resembles brown motor or '___ oil'.
items.exp: Adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma fluid has a classic 'machinery oil' appearance. (Book p950)

items.q: Assess the demographics of Rathke's cleft cyst: I It typically presents in the 4th to 6th decades of life. II It appears as a unilocular sellar mass that lacks calcification.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Rathke's cleft cyst presents in the 4th to 6th decade as a unilocular sellar mass without calcification. (Book p950)

items.q: Which step is NOT part of the diagnostic algorithm for acromegaly?
opts: Oral glucose suppression test (75 gm glucose)
Pituitary function testing for other hormonal axes
items.exp: The diagnostic flow uses IGF-1 screening, OGST confirmation, pituitary MRI, and pituitary function testing; water deprivation is for diabetes insipidus. (Book p950)
